value.title: Cross-model review round 3 (final) — claude-session-start-adopt
value.note:
SCOPE unchanged across all three rounds: read-only on code, writes confined to assets/reviews/, no daemon restarted, no real Claude settings written by this review. Final re-review of 5dc1cfae against round 2 (135fcc2c..HEAD).

GATES, RUN BY ME. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0. `cargo test -p pij-harnesses -p pij-cli` exit 0, 132 passed — the PM's figure, reproduced. `cargo test --workspace` exit 0, 546 passed. `shellcheck` exit 0. `just typecheck` exit 0. `cargo fmt --check` exit 0. Every claimed gate is green under my own hand, and the two new tests `duplicate_stale_managed_hooks_collapse_to_one` and `correct_managed_hook_removes_stale_sibling` are present and passing.

RED-FIRST, WITNESSED RATHER THAN TAKEN ON TRUST. I do not have to accept the PM's red-first claim, because I ran the same two cases myself on the previous tree and recorded the failures before this fix existed: round 2's receipt for shape TWO-stale-managed reads `STALE MANAGED PATH SURVIVES: ["/tmp/b/claude-session-start-pij.sh"]`, and shape stale-and-current-both returned `EnsurePlan::NoChange` with the stale entry intact. Those observations were made on 135fcc2c with the same instrument that now reports both cases clean on 5dc1cfae. The witness was observed to fail before it was observed to pass, by an instrument outside the code under test.

PROBE RE-RUN AND WIDENED. The out-of-tree property probe (path-dep on crates/harnesses; nothing written inside the repo) was rebuilt against 5dc1cfae and its invariants tightened to match the new contract: after any Write, exactly ONE managed command survives, it equals the expected path, every foreign command is unchanged in value and order, every foreign ENTRY survives, and re-planning the result yields NoChange. Run over 6 F7-targeted shapes, 3 entry-survival edges, and 12 regression shapes carried forward from rounds 1-2. Results: all F7 cases pass, all 9 valid regression shapes pass, the 3 invalid shapes refuse without writing, and one previously unfiled edge fails — F9. The inspect probe was re-run over 4 homes.

AC LEDGER, FINAL. AC1 TRUE. AC2 TRUE. AC3 TRUE. AC4 TRUE. AC5 TRUE. All five hold on evidence I generated rather than evidence I read.

FINDINGS ACROSS THE STREAM: 9 raised, 9 closed. 7 fixed, 2 refuted on their evidence (the F2 opt-out half and F8), 1 open at NIT (F9), none blocking.

value.finding: ROUND 2, NOW CLOSED, and fixed at the root rather than at the two cases I happened to name. The NoChange guard is now `managed_count == 1 && …contains(command)`, so 'already correct' can no longer short-circuit past a duplicate, and `reconcile_managed_hook_commands` sweeps the whole array with a `kept` latch: the first managed command is rewritten to the current path and every later managed command is removed. I probed six shapes, four of which I had not filed: two stale entries collapse to one; three stale plus an interleaved foreign entry collapse to one with the foreign entry in its original position; stale-then-correct and correct-then-stale both converge regardless of order; the same correct command duplicated inside one entry's hooks array collapses to one; and a managed hook sharing an entry with a foreign sibling keeps both, with only the managed command rewritten. Every case re-plans as NoChange, so the state converges instead of oscillating. The diagnostic half closed with it: `inspect` now reports `installed=false` for both two-stale and stale-plus-correct, so `doctor claude-hook` can no longer say `installed` while a dead path is still wired up — which was the part of F7 I cared about most.
value.receipt: out-of-tree probe on 5dc1cfae — two-stale, three-stale-plus-foreign, stale-and-current, current-then-stale, duplicate-correct-twice, managed-and-foreign-same-entry all ok (exactly one managed command after, foreign commands and entries unchanged, idempotent); inspect two-stale → installed=false, stale-and-current → installed=false, installed-clean → installed=true; cargo test -p pij-harnesses -p pij-cli → exit 0, 132 passed including duplicate_stale_managed_hooks_collapse_to_one and correct_managed_hook_removes_stale_sibling

value.finding: ROUND 2, REFUTED, AND I ACCEPT THE REFUTATION. The argument is correct on the contract, and I can check it rather than defer to it. AC4's byte-for-byte promise is written as 'existing hooks (Notification/PreToolUse/PostToolUse) preserved byte-for-byte' — it names the other event arrays, and those are exactly what the reconcile does not touch: I re-verified a sibling `PreToolUse` value passes through byte-identical alongside a reconciled SessionStart, as does an unrelated top-level `theme`. SessionStart is the array under reconciliation, so it is the one place a rewrite is the point rather than a side effect, and what a reader of that array is owed is semantic: foreign entries keep their values and their order, which my probe asserts on every reconcile shape and which held on all six. JSON whitespace and object key order are not promised anywhere in the plan, the impl-guide, or the AC text, and I should not have implied a contract that no document carries. I withdraw the finding. The residual is advice, not a defect: a migration reformats the SessionStart array, and one line in docs/how would stop the next person diffing their settings from thinking something went wrong. Take it or leave it — it is not a condition of ship.
value.receipt: probe shape stale-pretty on 5dc1cfae: sibling PreToolUse value and top-level theme byte-identical, SessionStart foreign entry values and order preserved, whitespace and key order rewritten; AC4 text read from plan.dd.md

value.finding: NEW, small, and worth one line because it contradicts a rule the impl-guide states outright ('Never remove or reorder existing hook entries'). `reconcile_managed_hook_commands` ends each iteration with `if !hooks.is_empty() { reconciled.push(entry) }`. That test is meant to drop an entry the sweep itself emptied, but it cannot tell that case apart from an entry that arrived empty: a foreign SessionStart entry written as `{"matcher":"resume","hooks":[]}` is silently deleted whenever any reconcile runs on that file. That this is an oversight rather than a decision is visible one branch up — an entry with NO `hooks` key at all takes the early `continue` and is preserved, so the intent to keep foreign entries is already expressed in the same function. Consequence is genuinely small: an entry with no hooks does nothing, so behaviour is unchanged and no AC moves. It is still someone's config line disappearing on a path they did not ask for and will not be told about, which is the shape of thing that gets discovered months later as 'pij ate my settings'.
value.receipt: out-of-tree probe shape foreign-entry-empty-hooks-array → FOREIGN ENTRY DROPPED: {"hooks":[],"matcher":"resume"}; sibling shape foreign-entry-no-hooks-key → entry preserved; append-path shape with the same empty entry and no managed command → entry preserved (the append path is unaffected)
value.note: Smallest fix, one line: capture `let was_empty = hooks.is_empty();` before `retain_mut`, then push when `was_empty || !hooks.is_empty()`. A test seeding a foreign empty-hooks entry next to a stale managed one, asserting the entry survives, would have caught it and belongs beside the two new managed_hook tests. Fine to ship without this.

value.rationale: Closed at the root, not at my two examples: I probed six shapes including four I never filed, and all converge to exactly one managed hook with foreign entries intact and idempotent re-plan. Red-first is witnessed rather than asserted — my own round-2 receipts record both cases failing on 135fcc2c with the same instrument that passes them now.

The refutation is right on the contract and I checked it rather than conceded it: AC4 names Notification/PreToolUse/PostToolUse, those arrays are untouched, and SessionStart's foreign entries keep their values and order. Whitespace and key order are promised by no document in this plan, so I withdraw a contract I implied and no one wrote. The docs/how note remains available as advice.

Found by probing the fix rather than the bug: an entry that arrived with an empty hooks array is indistinguishable, to this test, from one the sweep emptied, so a foreign entry is deleted. Behaviourally inert, one line to fix, and left to the PM's judgement — it does not hold up the merge.

FINAL VERDICT — APPROVE, ship it. All five acceptance criteria are true on evidence I generated: clippy 0, workspace tests 546 passed, targeted 132 passed, shellcheck 0, typecheck 0, fmt 0, plus 21 settings shapes driven through the planner from outside the crate. Across three rounds, nine findings were raised and nine are closed: seven fixed, two refuted on evidence I re-checked rather than on rank, one NIT open by choice. Two things to carry forward rather than fix here: G1 still says `pij adopt` where the code now correctly says `pij-rs adopt`, and F9 wants one line whenever the file is next open.
